# Golden expected-edges fixture: tests/fixtures/golden/python
#
# Format: one edge per line --
#   <source qualname> <EDGE_KIND> <target qualname | UNRESOLVED> [<resolution kind>]
#
# A line starting with `#` (after trimming) is a full-line comment and is
# ignored. A line may end with a trailing `# xfail: <why>` marker to record
# a known-failing edge: excluded from precision/recall, reported every run,
# and flagged loudly if it starts resolving correctly (see
# tests/common/golden.rs's module doc comment and ScoreboardReport).
#
# The optional trailing `<resolution kind>` column pins the exact tier
# (exact, import, receiver_type, inherited, two_segment, bare_name) that
# must have resolved the edge, not just its target -- see that same module
# doc for why. Present on every resolved line below: this fixture carries a
# same-named decoy for every target (see greeter.py's LoudGreeter,
# animals.py's Cat, other_module.py), so each shape can only pass through
# the resolution path it names.
#
# Scope: CALLS edges whose source is any symbol defined in this fixture's
# own files (not just the sources named below) count toward precision/
# recall (see tests/common/golden.rs's `compare`). CONTAINS, EXTENDS,
# IMPORTS, etc. are out of scope entirely, so they can't swamp the score.
#
# Baseline measured 2026-09-23: precision 1.0, recall 1.0 (8/8 CALLS
# edges). No known-failing lines today -- every required call shape in
# this fixture already resolves correctly, including with same-named
# decoys present for every resolved target.

# Plain call: a bare same-module function call. other_module.local_util is
# a same-named decoy in a different module.
caller.entry CALLS caller.local_util exact

# `from x import y` call: format_greeting is bound by name only, not
# through an attribute access on `helper`. other_module.format_greeting is
# a same-named decoy.
caller.call_imported_helper CALLS helper.format_greeting import

# Method call on self. greeter.LoudGreeter.format is a same-named decoy.
greeter.Greeter.greet CALLS greeter.Greeter.format exact

# Receiver-typed call: the annotated parameter `g: Greeter` pins the type.
# greeter.LoudGreeter.greet is a same-named decoy -- without receiver-type
# resolution actually gating the bind, this would go ambiguous (two
# `greet`s) rather than silently landing on the right one.
caller.call_receiver_typed CALLS greeter.Greeter.greet receiver_type

# Inherited method call: Dog declares no `speak` of its own -- must
# dispatch to Animal.speak via Dog's recorded EXTENDS edge.
# animals.Cat.speak is a same-named decoy -- without the inheritance tier
# actually gating the bind, this would go ambiguous (two `speak`s) rather
# than silently landing on the right one.
caller.call_inherited CALLS animals.Animal.speak inherited

# Ambiguous bare name: `run` is defined in two unrelated modules and
# imported from neither here -- must stay unresolved, not guess.
caller.call_ambiguous CALLS UNRESOLVED

# Call into an external library: `requests` is never indexed (it isn't
# part of this fixture repo), so this must stay unresolved.
caller.call_external CALLS UNRESOLVED

# Cross-file incoming call, for the incremental golden test: downstream.py
# imports and calls caller.entry, so the incremental scenario has a
# genuine incoming edge that must still resolve correctly after caller.py
# alone is re-synced (see golden_python.rs's incremental test doc for what
# that test actually verifies here).
downstream.use_entry CALLS caller.entry import
